appraisal_events.evidence: He questions Andrée "non sur un ton interrogatif mais comme si je l'avais su de tout temps", asks to be allowed to watch her caress Albertine's friends and is flatly refused ("pour rien au monde je ne ferais ce que vous dites devant vous"), sees himself as "l'aspect figé d'un animal autour duquel un cercle progressivement resserré est lentement décrit par l'oiseau fascinateur", and retreats with "Enfin soit, puisque vous ne voulez pas me le dire", preferring to seem to withhold a proof he does not have.
appraisal_events.explanation: The interrogation he had prepared collapses: he is the fascinated prey, his degrading request is refused, his bluff about the Buttes-Chaumont produces nothing, and he must cover an empty hand.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Elle avoua tout cela sans aucune difficulté, en souriant"; she denies everything concerning Albertine and swears to it; she catches his trap before he finishes his sentence, after which "tout ce que je verrais maintenant ne serait plus qu'arrangé facticement pour moi"; the narrator ends by calling her "dépositaire elle-même d'un secret qu'elle ne voulait pas livrer".
appraisal_events.explanation: Andrée owns the scene: she avows her own tastes without shame or damage, controls what is disclosed, sees the trap coming, and keeps the one thing he wants.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Andrée regrettait Albertine, mais je sentis tout de suite qu'elle ne lui manquait pas"; she yields Albertine up easily now, and Albertine has "perdu pour moi non seulement sa vie mais, rétrospectivement, un peu de sa réalité, puisque je voyais qu'elle n'était pas indispensable, unique pour Andrée qui avait pu la remplacer par d'autres"; she ends the passage as one term in a series of "substituts de plaisirs se remplaçant l'un l'autre en dégradations successives".
appraisal_events.explanation: A distinct movement of the passage takes reality away from the dead Albertine: she turns out not to have been indispensable even to her closest friend, and is placed in a graded series of interchangeable substitutes.

status_effects.explanation: He loses the interview he staged: his feigned omniscience, his proposition and his hazarded name all fail, and he must retire pretending to hold a proof he lacks.
She concedes her own tastes with a smile, costlessly, and still commands the exchange, denying, detecting the trap, and keeping her secret.
The dead Albertine loses standing retrospectively: not missed, replaceable for Andrée, and reduced to one degraded substitute in a series.

ambiguities: The narration explicitly leaves the value of Andrée's denial undecided — it calmed him, "mais peut-être était-elle dictée par le devoir ... de ne pas laisser croire ce qu'Albertine lui avait sans doute, pendant sa vie, demandé de nier" — so her testimony neither clears nor convicts Albertine here.
